nodes.name: Locally compact group G and closed subgroup H
nodes.statement: Let G be a locally compact group with left Haar measure $\mu$ and H a closed subgroup of $G$.

nodes.name: Homogeneous space G/H
nodes.statement: The left coset space $G/H$ is a homogeneous space with quotient topology.

nodes.name: Modular functions of G and H agree on H
nodes.statement: We assume that $\Delta_G(h)= \Delta_H(h),$ for all $h\in H,$ where $\Delta_G$ and $\Delta_H$ are the modular function of $G$ and $H$ respectively.

nodes.name: Rho function
nodes.statement: For the pair $(G,H),$ a rho function is  a continuous function $\rho: G \to (0,\infty)$ such that $\rho(gh)= \rho(g)$ for all $g\in G$ and $h\in H$(see \cite[p. 65]{fol}).
nodes.origin_citation: Folland, A course in abstract harmonic analysis

nodes.name: Unitary group of a Hilbert space
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{U}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ be the group consisting of all unitary operators on some Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$.

nodes.name: Continuous unitary representation of a homogeneous space
nodes.definiendum: continuous unitary representation of the homogeneous space $G/H$
nodes.statement_short: A map from G/H to unitaries, weakly continuous, multiplicative on cosets and with $\pi(g^{-1}H)=\pi(gH)^*$.

nodes.name: Square integrable representation of G/H
nodes.statement_short: $\pi$ is square integrable if some $\xi$ has finite positive weighted integral $C_\xi$ of $|\langle\xi,\pi(gH)\xi\rangle|^2$.

nodes.name: Admissibility constant C_xi
nodes.statement: C_{\xi} =  \int_{G/H} \frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}|\langle \xi, \pi(gH)\xi \rangle|^{2} d\mu_{G/H}(gH).
nodes.label: eq1

nodes.name: Admissible wavelet
nodes.statement: Then, $\xi$ satisfying (\ref{eq1}) is called an admissible wavelet.

nodes.name: Continuous wavelet transform on a homogeneous space
nodes.statement_short: $W_\xi\eta(gH)$ is the $\rho$-weighted inner product of $\eta$ with $\pi(gH)\xi$.

nodes.name: Boundedness of the wavelet transform into L^2(G/H)
nodes.statement: If $\pi$ is irreducible, then $W_{\xi}$ is a bounded linear operator from Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi} \text{ into } L^2(G/H)$ and $ L^2(G/H) \simeq L^2(G/H, d\mu_{G/H}),$ where $\mu_{G/H}$ is  a relatively $G$-invariant measure on $G/H$ which arises from the rho function $\rho.$
conclusions: $W_{\xi}$ is a bounded linear operator from Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi} \text{ into } L^2(G/H)$
nodes.statement_short: For irreducible $\pi$, $W_\xi$ maps $\mathcal{H}_\pi$ boundedly into $L^2$ of the relatively invariant measure on $G/H$.

nodes.name: Range of the wavelet transform is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space
nodes.statement: Also, $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with pointwise bounded kernel and the operator ${C_{\xi}}^{-1/2}W_{\xi}$  is an isometry.
conclusions: $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with pointwise bounded kernel

nodes.name: H compact and trivial rho function
nodes.statement: Throughout this section, we assume that $H$ is compact and $\rho(g) = 1$ for all $g \in G$.

nodes.name: G-invariance of the quotient measure
nodes.statement: Thus, $\mu_{G/H} $ is a $G$-invariant measure, i.e. $d\mu_{G/H}(saH) = d\mu_{G/H}(aH)$ for all $s\in G$ and $aH\in G/H$.

nodes.name: Continuity of the measure of intersections with translates
nodes.statement: If $ M_{0}\subseteq M \subseteq G/H$ are such that $ \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty,$ then the function $h: G \to [0,\infty) $ such that $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_{0})$, is continuous.
assumptions: $ M_{0}\subseteq M \subseteq G/H$ are such that $ \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty,$
conclusions: the function $h: G \to [0,\infty) $ such that $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_{0})$, is continuous
nodes.label: cont

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement:
Let  $C_{00}(G/H)$ be the space of continuous functions with compact support. Since $\chi_{M_0} \in L^1(G/H)$ and $C_{00}(G/H)$  is dense in $L^{1}(G/H),$ therefore we  choose $f \in C_{00}(G/H)$ such that $\| \chi_{M_0} - f \|_{1} < \epsilon$, where $ \epsilon > 0$ is arbitrary. Then, we consider
\begin{flalign*}
|h(a)-h(b)| &\leq \int_{G/H} \left|\left(\chi_{aM_0} - {}_af\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\
&\qquad + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af-{}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\
&\qquad +  \int_{G/H} \left|\left({}_bf -\chi_{bM_0}\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\
&= 2\|\chi_{M_0} - f \|_1 + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af-  {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH) &\\
& < 2\epsilon + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af- {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH).
\end{flalign*}

\noindent   The map $a \to  {}_af$ is  continuous  from $G \to (C_{00}(G/H), \|\cdot\|_{\infty})$ \cite[Proposition 1.25]{kan:13}, where ${}_af(xH) = f(a^{-1}xH)$ for all $a\in G$ and $xH \in G/H$. Hence, $h$ is a continuous function.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $\chi_{M_0}$ in $L^1$ by a compactly supported continuous $f$ and use continuity of translation $a\mapsto {}_af$.

nodes.name: Translate enlarging a finite-measure set by less than epsilon
assumptions: $G_0$, the identity component of $G$ be non-compact
nodes.statement_short: With non-compact identity component, some translate $aM_0$ ($a\in G_0$) enlarges $M$ strictly but by less than $\epsilon$ in measure.
nodes.label: conn

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement:
Define $h: G_0 \to \mathbb{R}^+$ by $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}).$ Since $\mu_{G/H}$ is $G$-invariant, therefore $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M)+\mu_{G/H}(M_0) - \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_0).$ Then by  Lemma \ref{cont}, $h$ is a continuous function. Also $\mu_{G/H}$ is regular, so there exists a compact subset $K$ of $M$ such that $\mu_{G/H}(M\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$ Let $K = \{xH: x\in E \}$, where $E$ is a compact subset of $G$. Thus, $S = EHE^{-1}$ is a compact subset of $G$. Choose $a \in G_0\setminus S.$ For such a choice of $a,$ we have $ aK \cap K = \phi$. Moreover,
\begin{align*}
aM_0\cap K
&= a(M_0 \cap (K \cup K^{'}))\cap K\\
&= (aM_0 \cap aK \cap K)\cup (a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K)\\
&= a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K \subseteq a(M_0 \cap K^{'}). 
\end{align*} 
Therefore, it follows that
$$\mu_{G/H}(aM_0 \cap K)\leq \mu_{G/H}(a(M_0\cap K^{'}))=  \mu_{G/H}(M_0\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$$ 
Again, we have
\begin{flalign*}
 h(a)&= \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_0) &\\
&= \mu_{G/H}((M\cap K)\cup (M\cap K^{'})\cup (aM_0\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'}))&\\
&\geq \mu_{G/H}( (M\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'})) &\\
&= \mu_{G/H}(M)- \mu_{G/H}(M\cap K^{'})+ \mu_{G/H}(aM_0)- \mu_{G/H}(aM_0\cap K)&\\
&> \mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e). 
\end{flalign*} 
Thus, $h$ is a non-constant continuous function on the connected set $G_{0}$. So, we can choose $a \in G_{0}$ such that 
\begin{align*}
\mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e) < h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}) < \mu_{G/H}(M)+\epsilon = h(e)+ \epsilon.\hspace{1cm}\qedhere
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: $h(a)=\mu(M\cup aM_0)$ is continuous by Lemma 2.1; choosing $a$ outside a compact set gives $h(a)>h(e)$, and connectedness of $G_0$ gives intermediate values.

nodes.name: Support of the wavelet transform has infinite measure
nodes.statement: Let $G$ and $H$ be as in Lemma \ref{conn} and $\xi $ be an admissible wavelet associated with an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$.  Then for any $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi} \setminus \{0\}$, the set $\{gH\in G/H: W_{\xi}\eta(gH)\neq 0 \}$ has infinite measure.
assumptions: $\xi $ be an admissible wavelet associated with an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$
conclusions: for any $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi} \setminus \{0\}$, the set $\{gH\in G/H: W_{\xi}\eta(gH)\neq 0 \}$ has infinite measure
nodes.statement_short: For non-zero $\eta$, $W_\xi\eta$ is non-zero on a set of infinite measure in $G/H$.
nodes.label: concth

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2.3
nodes.statement:
It is enough to show that for every subset $M$ of $ G/H$ with $\mu_{G/H}(M)< \infty $, the set $
\{ F \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}): F = \chi_{M} F \} = \{0\}$.
For this assume that $M \subset G/H$ and $0\neq F_{0} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ with $F_0 = \chi_{M}F_0.$ Let $M_0 = \{xH \in G/H : F_{0}(xH)\neq 0 \}$. Then, 
 $$0 < \mu_{G/H}(M_0) \leq \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty.$$ By Lemma \ref{conn}, there exists $a^{(1)} \in G_0 $ satisfying 
\[
\mu_{G/H}(M) < \mu_{G/H}(M \cup a^{(1)}M_0) < \mu_{G/H}(M) + \frac{\epsilon}{2}. 
\]
Take $M_1=M$ and $M_2 = M_1 \cup a^{(1)}M_0$ and again using  Lemma \ref{conn}, there exists $a^{(2)} \in G_0 $ satisfying 
\begin{align*}
\mu_{G/H}(M_2) < \mu_{G/H}(M_2 \cup a^{(2)}a^{(1)}M_0) < \mu_{G/H}(M_2) + \frac{\epsilon}{2^2}.
\end{align*}
 Continuing in the same manner, we get an increasing sequence $\{M_k\}_{k=1}^{\infty}$ of subsets of $G/H$ given by $$M_k = M_{k-1}\cup a^{(k-1)}\cdots a^{2}a^{1}M_0,$$  where  $a^{(i)} \in G_0$ for all $i = 1,2,\dots,k-1$ and satisfy
\begin{align} \mu_{G/H}(M_k)< \mu_{G/H}(M_k\cup a^{(k)}a^{(k-1)}\cdots a^{(1)}M_0)< \mu_{G/H}(M_k)+\frac{\epsilon}{2^k}.
\end{align}
Define $S = \bigcup\limits_{k=1}^{\infty} M_k.$ Then,
\begin{align*}
\mu_{G/H}(S) &= \lim\limits_{k \to \infty}\mu_{G/H}(M_k)
\leq \lim\limits_{k \to \infty } \left(\mu_{G/H}(M_{k-1})+ \frac{\epsilon}{2^{(k-1)}}\right)\\
&\leq  \mu_{G/H}(M)+ \lim\limits_{k \to \infty } \sum\limits_{i=1}^{k-1}\frac{\epsilon}{2^i}
=\mu_{G/H}(M)+ \epsilon < \infty.
\end{align*}
Consider the family $\{F_{k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ of functions on $G/H$ as follows
\begin{flalign*}
&&&F_{1}(aH)= F_0(aH) &\\
&&&F_{k}(aH) = F_{k-1}((a^{k-1})^{-1}aH) \quad \text{for all } k \geq 2,\text{ and }   aH \in G/H.
\end{flalign*}
We will show by induction  that $F_{k}\in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ for all $k \in \mathbb{N}.$ Clearly, $F_1 = F_0 \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}).$ Let us  assume that $F_{k-1} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}),\ \text{i.e.}\  F_{k-1} = W_{\xi}(\eta)$ for some $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}.$ Then,
\begin{align*}
F_{k}(aH) &= W_{\xi}(\eta)((a^{(k-1)})^{-1}aH)\\
&=\left\langle \eta , \pi((a^{(k-1)})^{-1}aH)\xi \right\rangle\\
&= \left\langle \pi(a^{(k-1)}H)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi \right\rangle\\
&= W_{\xi}(\pi({a^{(k-1)}H)}\eta)
\end{align*}
which implies that $F_{k} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}).$ Using (\ref{lin-ind}), we conclude that the family $\{F_{k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ of functions on $G/H$ is linearly independent vanishing outside the set $S$ of finite measure.
Since $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel, therefore each subspace of $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}) $ consisting of functions having support 
 on a set of finite measure must be of finite dimension \cite{Wilc:00}. If $W_{\xi}\eta \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ such that $\mu_{G/H}\{xH : W_{\xi}\eta(xH)\neq 0 \}< \infty, $ then $W_{\xi}\eta = 0$ a.e. and hence $\eta = 0.$
Thus, the support of $W_{\xi}\eta$ is a set of infinite measure for every non-zero $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Iterating Lemma 2.2 builds infinitely many linearly independent translates supported in a finite-measure set, impossible in a RKHS with bounded kernel. Key step: the translates $F_k$ stay in $W_\xi(\mathcal{H}_\pi)$ by induction.

nodes.name: Measure bound for the k-th enlargement
nodes.statement: \mu_{G/H}(M_k)< \mu_{G/H}(M_k\cup a^{(k)}a^{(k-1)}\cdots a^{(1)}M_0)< \mu_{G/H}(M_k)+\frac{\epsilon}{2^k}.
nodes.label: lin-ind

nodes.name: Remarks on the necessity of irreducibility and abelian groups
nodes.statement_short: Without irreducibility the support can be compact (regular rep.); for abelian $G$ the support is $G$, but it can have small measure for non-abelian compact $G$.

nodes.name: Groups with square integrable irreducible representations
nodes.statement:
1. Groups of the type $ H \ltimes \mathbb{R}^n ,$ where $H$ is a closed subgroup of $GL_n(R).$
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]

\item Let $G =  A  \ltimes \mathbb{R}^2$, where 
$A = \left \{ \begin{pmatrix}
a_1 & 0\\
0 & a_2 
\end{pmatrix} : a_1,a_2 \in \mathbb{R}^* \right\}$.\\
 A  square integrable irreducible representation $\pi$ of $G$ on $L^2(R^2)$ is given by
 $$\pi\left[ \begin{pmatrix}
a_1 & 0\\
0 & a_2
\end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix}
 x_1\\
 x_2
\end{pmatrix}\right] g \begin{pmatrix}
y_1\\
y_2
\end{pmatrix} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{|a_1a_2|}}g\begin{pmatrix}
(y_1-x_1)/a_1\\ (y_2 -x_2)/a_2
\end{pmatrix}.$$
Also, $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is admissible if and only if 
$ C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^2} \Big| \frac{\widehat{\psi}(\gamma_1,\gamma_2)}{\sqrt{|\gamma_1\gamma_2|}}\Big|^2 d\gamma_1 d\gamma_2$ $ < \infty$  \cite{Dav:96}.

\item $G =A \ltimes \mathbb{R}^2 ,$ where $A = \left\{\begin{pmatrix}
a & b\\
0 & 1
\end{pmatrix}:a\in \mathbb{R}^*,b\in \mathbb{R}\right\}$.\\
 A square integrable irreducible representation $\pi$ on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by  
$$\pi\left[ \begin{pmatrix}
a & b\\
0 & 1
\end{pmatrix}, \begin{pmatrix}
 x\\
 y
\end{pmatrix} \right] g(u,v) = a^{-1}g\left(
a^{-1}(u-x+b(v-y)), v-y\right).$$
Also, $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is admissible if and only if  $ C_{\psi}=\int_{\mathbb{R}^2}\frac{|\widehat{\psi}(\xi_1,\xi_2)|^2}{|\xi_1|^2}d\xi_1d\xi_2 < \infty.$
\item  Shear group $\mathcal{S} = (\mathbb{R}^{*} \ltimes \mathbb{R}^{n-1})\ltimes \mathbb{R}^{n} \text{ for } n\geq 2 $ with group operation
$(a,s,t).(a',s',t') = (aa',s+|a|^{1-1/n}s^{'}, t+S_s A_a t'),$ where
 $$
 A_a = \begin{pmatrix}
 a & 0_{n-1}^T \\
 0_{n-1} & sgn(a)|a|^{1/n}I_{n-1} 
\end{pmatrix}  \text{ and }
S_s = \begin{pmatrix}
1 & s^{T}\\
0_{n-1} & I_{n-1}
\end{pmatrix}.$$
A square integrable irreducible representation $\pi$ on $L^2{(\mathbb{R}^n)}$ is given by 
$$\pi(a,s,t)f(x) = |a|^{\frac{1}{2n}-1}f(A_a^{-1}S_s^{-1}(x-t))$$ and function $\psi \in L^2(\mathbb{R}^2) $ is admissible if and only if $C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \frac{|\widehat{\psi}(\omega)|^2}{|\omega_1|^n} d\omega < \infty$ \cite{dah;10}.
\end{enumerate}
2. Low dimensional nilpotent Lie groups.
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item Reduced Weyl Heisenberg group, $ \mathbb{R}^{n} \ltimes (\mathbb{R}^{n} \times \mathbb{T})\text{ for } n\in \mathbb{N}$ with the group operation $(a_1, b_1,t_1)(a_2,b_2,t_2) = (a_1+a_2, b_1+b_2, t_1 t_2e^{2\pi i a_1\cdot b_2}).$
An irreducible square integrable representation $\sigma$ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ is given by 
$$\sigma(a,b,t)f(x)= te^{2\pi i b(x-a)}f(x-a).$$
Every $\psi \in L^2(R^n)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.
\end{enumerate}

\noindent For the group structure of 5-dimensional groups $G_{5,1}, G_{5,3},G_{5,6}$ given below (see \cite{Niel:83}).
\begin{enumerate}[(i)]
\item [(ii)] $G_{5,1}/\mathbb{Z},$ an irreducible square integrable  representation $ \sigma $ on the  Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by 
$$\sigma(t,x_2\dots , x_5)f(s_1,s_2) = te^{-2\pi i(x_2s_1+x_4s_2)}f(s_1-x_3,s_2-x_5),$$
where $t\in \mathbb{T}, x_i \in \mathbb{R}.$ 
Every $\psi \in L^2(R^2)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.
\item [(iii)] $G_{5,3}/\mathbb{Z},$ a square integrable irreducible representation $ \sigma $ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by 
$$ \text{ } \qquad \sigma(t,x_2\dots , x_5)f(s_1,s_2) = te^{-2\pi i(x_3x_4 -x_5s_1+x_2s_2-\frac{1}{2}x_4s_2^2)}f(s_1-x_3,s_2-x_5),$$
where $t\in \mathbb{T}, x_i \in \mathbb{R}.$ 
Every $\psi \in L^2(R^2)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.
\item[(iv)]  $G_{5,6}/\mathbb{Z},$ an irreducible square integrable representation $ \sigma $ on the Hilbert space $ L^2(\mathbb{R}^2)$ is given by 
\begin{align*} 
\quad \sigma(t,x_2\dots , x_5)f(s_1,s_2) \\
 = t\exp2\pi i&\left( -\frac{1}{2}x_4^2x_5-\frac{1}{6}x_4x_5^3\right.-x_3s_1-x_4x_5+\frac{1}{6}x_5^3s_1\\
 &-\frac{1}{2}x_5s_1^2-x_2s_2+\frac{1}{2}x_4x_5^2s_2+\frac{1}{2}x_5^3s_2^2\\
 & -\frac{1}{2}x_4x_5\left.-\frac{1}{2}x_5^2s_1s_2+\frac{1}{2x_5s_1s_2^2} \right)f(s_1-x_4,s_2-x_5),
\end{align*}
where $t\in \mathbb{T}, x_i \in \mathbb{R}.$ 
Every $\psi \in L^2(R^2)$ is an admissible wavelet and $C_{\psi} = \|\psi\|_2^2$.
\end{enumerate}
3. Let $A$ be a locally compact group  with non-compact identity component having a square integrable irreducible representation $\sigma$ and $B$ be a compact group of the form $H\rtimes K$. Let $\tau$ be an irreducible representation of $B$ which is identity on $K$. Then, $ G = (A \times B)/({\{0\}\times K})$ has an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi = \sigma \otimes \tau$, where $\otimes $ being the outer tensor product \cite[Theorem 7.17]{fol}.
nodes.statement_short: Examples: affine-type groups $H\ltimes\mathbb{R}^n$, shear group, reduced Weyl-Heisenberg and 5-dimensional nilpotent groups, and quotients of products.
nodes.label: eg

nodes.name: Admissible pair
nodes.statement:
For an  irreducible unitary representation $\pi$ of $G/H$ with representation space $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$, 
a pair $ (\xi_1, \xi_2) $ consisting of admissible wavelets in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ is said to be an admissible pair if
$\langle \xi_1, \xi_2 \rangle \neq 0$ and $$C_{\xi_1
\xi_2} = \frac{1}{\langle \xi_1,\xi_2 \rangle}\int_{G/H}W_{\xi_1}(\xi_1)(gH)\ \overline{W_{\xi_2}(\xi_2)(gH)}\ d\mu_{G/H}(gH) $$ is a non-zero scalar.
nodes.genus: a pair $ (\xi_1, \xi_2) $ consisting of admissible wavelets in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$
nodes.statement_short: Two admissible wavelets with non-orthogonal inner product whose cross admissibility constant $C_{\xi_1\xi_2}$ is non-zero.

nodes.name: Intertwining of W_{xi_2}^* W_{xi_1}
nodes.statement:
As proved in \cite[Theorem 2.1]{kam:12}, for admissible wavelets $\xi_1,\xi_2$,
 the operator  $ W_{\xi_2}^*W_{\xi_1}$ intertwines with $\pi$.

nodes.name: Derivation of the reconstruction formula for an admissible pair
nodes.statement_short: By Schur's lemma $W_{\xi_2}^*W_{\xi_1}=cI$; evaluating at $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ identifies $c$ with $C_{\xi_1\xi_2}$.

nodes.name: Weak reconstruction formula for an admissible pair
nodes.statement:
If $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ is an admissible pair, then 
$\langle \eta_1,\eta_2 \rangle= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\langle W_{\xi_1}\eta_1, W_{\xi_2}\eta_2 \rangle$ which further implies that every 
 $\eta\in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ can be decomposed as 
\begin{align*}
\eta &= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{G/H}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(g)}\right)^{1/2}W_{\xi_1}\eta(gH)\ \pi(gH)\xi_2\ d\mu(gH),
\end{align*}
where  the integral is defined in the weak sense.
nodes.statement_short: An admissible pair gives $\eta=C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int W_{\xi_1}\eta(gH)\pi(gH)\xi_2$ weakly.

nodes.name: Homogeneous approximation property
nodes.statement:
An admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ is said to have homogeneous approximation property in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$, if for any $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $\epsilon > 0,$ there exists some compact subset $K$ of $G/H$ such that every compact subset $K^{'}$ of $G/H$ with $K \subseteq K^{'}$ satisfies
$$\left\|\pi(sH)\eta - C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)^{1/2}W_{\xi_1}\pi(sH)\eta(aH)\ \pi(aH)\xi_2\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\right\|\leq \epsilon,$$
for all $s \in G.$
nodes.statement_short: Truncating the reconstruction integral to a translated large compact set approximates every translate $\pi(sH)\eta$ uniformly in $s$.

nodes.name: Homogeneous approximation property of admissible pairs
nodes.statement: Let $G/H$ be a $\sigma $-compact homogeneous space with  an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$. Then every admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ possesses homogeneous approximation property in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$.
assumptions: $G/H$ be a $\sigma $-compact homogeneous space with  an irreducible square integrable representation $\pi$
conclusions: every admissible pair $(\xi_1,\xi_2)$ possesses homogeneous approximation property in $\mathcal{H}_{\pi}$

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.2
nodes.statement_short: Bound the truncation error by the tail integral of $|W_{\xi_1}\eta|^2$ outside $K$ via Cauchy-Schwarz and invariance, then make it small by $\sigma$-compactness and dominated convergence.

nodes.name: Similitude group
nodes.statement:
We now  consider similitude group $ G=(\mathbb{R}^+\times S0(n))\ltimes \mathbb{R}^n,$ with group operation 
$$(a,r_{\theta},t)(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1) = (aa_1,r_{\theta}{r_{\theta}}_1, t+ ar_{\theta}t_1 ). $$

nodes.name: Square integrable representation of the similitude group
nodes.statement:
The mapping $\pi: G \to \mathcal{U}(L^2(\mathbb{R}^n))$ defined by
$$\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x) = a^{-n/2} \psi\left(r_{\theta}^{-1}\left(\frac{x-t}{a}\right)\right)$$ is a square integrable irreducible representation of $G$.
nodes.statement_short: The dilation-rotation-translation representation of the similitude group on $L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$.

nodes.name: Admissibility constant on the similitude group is independent of omega
nodes.statement: For $\psi\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, $$C_{\psi} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{+}}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{\widehat{|\psi}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))|^2}{a}\ da\ d\theta,$$ is  independent of almost every  $\omega \in \mathbb{R}^n$ (see \cite{ali;00}).

nodes.name: Cross admissibility constant on the similitude group
nodes.statement:
Also, for an admissible pair $(\psi_1,\psi_2)$,
$$C_{\psi_1\psi_2} = \int_{\mathbb{R}^{+}}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{\overline{\widehat{\psi_1}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}{a}\ da\ d\theta$$ 
is independent of $\omega$ upto a measure zero set.
conclusions: is independent of $\omega$ upto a measure zero set

nodes.name: Fourier transform of the truncated reconstruction
nodes.statement_short: The scale-truncated reconstruction $f_{A_1A_2}$ lies in $L^2$ and is a Fourier multiplier applied to $f$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.3
nodes.statement:
First we show that $f_{A_1A_2}$ is well defined. For this, we compute
\begin{align*}
&\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
&\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|^2dt \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
&\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\psi_2\|_{2}\ \frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
&\leq \|\psi_2\|_{2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 \frac{ dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)^{1/2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}} \right)^{1/2}\\
&=\|\psi_2\|_{2}\sqrt{C_{\psi_1}}\|f\|_2\ n^{-\frac{1}{2}}(A_1^{-n}-A_2^{-n})< \infty.
\end{align*}
Let $g\in  L^1\cap L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$ be arbitrary. Then 
\begin{align*}
&\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \left|g(x)f_{A_1A_2}(x)\right|dx \\
&\leq \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(|g(x)| \int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} |\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)|\frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}    \right)dx\\
& < \infty.
\end{align*}
Thus, using Tonneli theorem, the function  $g(\cdot)\langle f, \pi(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)\psi_1\rangle \pi(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)\psi_2(\cdot) $ is integrable.
Again, we have
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_{A_1A_2}(x)\overline{g(x)}\ dx \\
 &= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)dx\\
 &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)dx\right)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
 &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}.
 \end{align*}
 Thus, 
 \begin{flalign*}
 \left|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_{A_1A_2}(x)\overline{g(x)}\ dx\right|
& \leq C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^+}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}| \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle|\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}&\\
&\leq  C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\|f\|_2C_{\psi_1}C_{\psi_2}\|g\|_2.
 \end{flalign*}
Therefore, by  Riesz representation theorem $f_{A_1A_2}\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n).$ 
Now on using Plancherel Theorem, we have
\begin{align*}
&&&\langle f_{A_1A_2}, g\rangle &\\
 &&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} & \\
&&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} (f*\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_1^{\star}(t))\ (g*\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_2^{\star}(t))\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} &\\
&&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\widehat{f}(\omega)\ \widehat{\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\ \psi_1^{\star}}(\omega)\ \overline{\widehat{g}(\omega)}\ \overline{\widehat{\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_2^{\star}}}(\omega)\ \frac{d\omega d\theta da}{a^{n+1}} &\\
&&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\widehat{f}(\omega) \left( \int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\overline{\widehat{\psi_1}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \frac{da d\theta}{a} \right) \overline{\widehat{g}(\omega)} d\omega.
\end{align*}
Since $g \in L^{1}\cap L^2(\mathbb{R}^n)$, therefore we have
\begin{align*}
\widehat{f_{A_1A_2}}(\omega) = C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\widehat{f}(\omega)\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)} \widehat{\psi_{1}}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\frac{dad\theta}{a}.\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad\qedhere
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Absolute convergence via Cauchy-Schwarz, $L^2$ membership via Tonelli and the Riesz representation theorem, then Plancherel yields the Fourier formula.

nodes.name: Pointwise homogeneous approximation property on the similitude group
conclusions: for any $\epsilon,p > 0$, there exist $A_2 > A_1 > 0 $ such that for any $(a,r_{\theta},t) \in G$ with $0< p\leq a$ and $0 < A_1^{'}\leq A_1$, $A_2^{'} \geq A_2,$  the following holds

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 3.4
nodes.statement_short: Bound the sup-norm error by $L^1$ norms of Fourier transforms of the small- and large-scale tails, which vanish by admissibility and dominated convergence.

nodes.name: Small-scale tail bound
nodes.statement: \int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}\leq C_{\psi_1}C_{\psi_2}< \infty

nodes.name: Large-scale tail bound

nodes.name: Type I groups A, B and action tau
nodes.statement: Let $A$ and $B$ be  locally compact, second countable, unimodular, group of type I and $\tau$ be a map from $B$ to $\text{Aut(A)},$ where $\text{Aut}(A)$ is a group of automorphism of $A$.

nodes.name: Left Haar measure on B x_tau A and the homomorphism delta_tau
nodes.statement: The left Haar measure $\mu$ on $G$ is given by $d\mu(b,a)=  \delta_{\tau}(b)\ da\ db$, where $\delta_{\tau}$ is a positive homomorphism of $B$ satisfying  $d(a) = \delta_{\tau}(b)\ d(\tau_{b}(a)).$

nodes.name: Quasi-regular representation of B x_tau A on L^2(A)
nodes.statement:
Define a representation $\pi$ of $G$ on  Hilbert space $L^2(A)$ such that
$$\pi(b,a)f(x)= f_{ba}(x)= \delta_{\tau}(b)^{1/2}f(\tau_{b^{-1}}(a^{-1}x)).$$

differentia: there exists a constant $0< C_{\psi} < \infty$ such that for almost every $\gamma \in \widehat{A}$ and for  all $f,g \in L^1\cap L^2(A)$
nodes.statement_short: $\psi$ is feasible if integrating its dilated Fourier transforms over $B$ multiplies traces by a fixed constant $C_\psi$.

nodes.name: Admissibility constant for abelian A
nodes.statement:
It may be noted that if $A$ is a locally compact abelian group, then for a  feasible wavelet $\psi$, 
$$C_{\psi}= \int_{B}|\widehat{\psi}(\gamma \circ \tau_{b})|^2 db,$$
is independent of almost every $\gamma\in \widehat{A}. $
For the case when $A$ is a locally compact abelian group, one may refer to \cite{fas;03}.

assumptions: $A$ is a locally compact abelian group

nodes.name: Continuous wavelet transform on B x_tau A
nodes.statement:
The continuous wavelet transform with respect to a feasible wavelet $\psi$ is an operator $W_{\psi}:L^2(A)\to L^2(G)$ defined as
$W_{\psi}f(b,a)= \langle f,\pi(b,a)\psi\rangle.$
nodes.section: 4 Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$

nodes.name: Wavelet transform as a convolution
nodes.statement:
Also,
$$W_{\psi}f(b,a)=\int_{A}f(x)\overline{ \delta_{\tau}(b)^{1/2}\psi(\tau_{b^{-1}}(a^{-1}x))}dx = \delta_{\tau}(b)^{1/2}f*(\psi\circ\tau_{b^{-1}})^{\star}(a),$$
where $(\psi\circ\tau_{b^{-1}})^{\star}(x)=\overline{(\psi\circ\tau_{b^{-1}})(x^{-1})}$.

nodes.statement: Using feasibility condition and  Plancherel's  theorem \cite[Theorem 7.36]{fol} for locally compact, unimodular, type I groups, one can show the following result:

nodes.statement_short: Feasibility condition combined with Plancherel's theorem for unimodular type I groups.

nodes.name: Isometry property of the wavelet transform
nodes.statement:
Let $\psi$ be a feasible wavelet and $f,g\in L^2(A)$. Then 
$\langle W_{\psi}f,W_{\psi}g\rangle = C_{\psi}\langle f,g \rangle$.

assumptions: $\psi$ be a feasible wavelet and $f,g\in L^2(A)$

nodes.name: Reproducing kernel of the wavelet range
nodes.statement:
In fact, one can show that $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel $k$ given by 
$$k((b,a),(b',a'))= \frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\langle \psi_{b'a'}, \psi_{ba}\rangle. $$
nodes.section: 4 Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
conclusions: $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel $k$

nodes.statement: Proceeding as in Lemma \ref{conn} and Theorem \ref{concth}, we obtain the following:

nodes.name: Support of wavelet transform on B x_tau A has infinite measure
nodes.statement: Let  $G = B\ltimes_{\tau} A$ be an abstract wavelet group with $A_0$ non compact and $\psi \in L^2(A)$ be a feasible wavelet. If $0\neq f \in L^2(A)$, then  the set $\{ (b,a):W_{\psi}f(b,a) \neq 0\} $ has infinite measure.

& \geq \|W_{\psi}f\| - \|P_MP_R\|\ \|W_{\psi}f\|\\

nodes.name: Integrated Heisenberg inequality

nodes.name: Choose approximant
nodes.statement: Let  $C_{00}(G/H)$ be the space of continuous functions with compact support. Since $\chi_{M_0} \in L^1(G/H)$ and $C_{00}(G/H)$  is dense in $L^{1}(G/H),$ therefore we  choose $f \in C_{00}(G/H)$ such that $\| \chi_{M_0} - f \|_{1} < \epsilon$, where $ \epsilon > 0$ is arbitrary.
nodes.statement_short: Approximate $\chi_{M_0}$ in $L^1$ by $f\in C_{00}$

nodes.name: Triangle inequality
nodes.statement:
Then, we consider
\begin{flalign*}
|h(a)-h(b)| &\leq \int_{G/H} \left|\left(\chi_{aM_0} - {}_af\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\
&\qquad + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af-{}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\
&\qquad +  \int_{G/H} \left|\left({}_bf -\chi_{bM_0}\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH)&\\
&= 2\|\chi_{M_0} - f \|_1 + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af-  {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH) &\\
& < 2\epsilon + \int_{M} \left|\left({}_af- {}_bf\right)(xH)\right|d\mu_{G/H}(xH).
\end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound $|h(a)-h(b)|$ via triangle inequality

nodes.name: Continuity of translation
nodes.statement: The map $a \to  {}_af$ is  continuous  from $G \to (C_{00}(G/H), \|\cdot\|_{\infty})$ \cite[Proposition 1.25]{kan:13}, where ${}_af(xH) = f(a^{-1}xH)$ for all $a\in G$ and $xH \in G/H$.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of translation in sup norm

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Hence, $h$ is a continuous function.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude continuity of $h$

nodes.name: Define h
nodes.statement: Define $h: G_0 \to \mathbb{R}^+$ by $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_{0}).$ Since $\mu_{G/H}$ is $G$-invariant, therefore $h(a) = \mu_{G/H}(M)+\mu_{G/H}(M_0) - \mu_{G/H}(M\cap aM_0).$
nodes.statement_short: Define $h(a)=\mu(M\cup aM_0)$ and expand by invariance

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.1
nodes.statement: Then by  Lemma \ref{cont}, $h$ is a continuous function.
nodes.statement_short: Continuity of $h$ by Lemma 2.1

nodes.name: Choose translate
nodes.statement: Also $\mu_{G/H}$ is regular, so there exists a compact subset $K$ of $M$ such that $\mu_{G/H}(M\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$ Let $K = \{xH: x\in E \}$, where $E$ is a compact subset of $G$. Thus, $S = EHE^{-1}$ is a compact subset of $G$. Choose $a \in G_0\setminus S.$ For such a choice of $a,$ we have $ aK \cap K = \phi$.
nodes.statement_short: Pick compact $K$ by regularity and $a$ outside $EHE^{-1}$ so $aK\cap K=\emptyset$

nodes.name: Bound overlap
nodes.statement:
Moreover,
\begin{align*}
aM_0\cap K
&= a(M_0 \cap (K \cup K^{'}))\cap K\\
&= (aM_0 \cap aK \cap K)\cup (a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K)\\
&= a(M_0 \cap K^{'})\cap K \subseteq a(M_0 \cap K^{'}). 
\end{align*} 
Therefore, it follows that
$$\mu_{G/H}(aM_0 \cap K)\leq \mu_{G/H}(a(M_0\cap K^{'}))=  \mu_{G/H}(M_0\setminus K) < \mu_{G/H}(M_0)/2.$$
nodes.statement_short: Bound $\mu(aM_0\cap K)<\mu(M_0)/2$

nodes.name: h non-constant
nodes.statement:
Again, we have
\begin{flalign*}
 h(a)&= \mu_{G/H}(M\cup aM_0) &\\
&= \mu_{G/H}((M\cap K)\cup (M\cap K^{'})\cup (aM_0\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'}))&\\
&\geq \mu_{G/H}( (M\cap K)\cup ( aM_{0}\cap K^{'})) &\\
&= \mu_{G/H}(M)- \mu_{G/H}(M\cap K^{'})+ \mu_{G/H}(aM_0)- \mu_{G/H}(aM_0\cap K)&\\
&> \mu_{G/H}(M) = h(e). 
\end{flalign*}
nodes.statement_short: Show $h(a)>h(e)$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Intermediate value on connected $G_0$

nodes.name: Reduction
nodes.statement:
It is enough to show that for every subset $M$ of $ G/H$ with $\mu_{G/H}(M)< \infty $, the set $
\{ F \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}): F = \chi_{M} F \} = \{0\}$.
nodes.statement_short: Reduce to: no non-zero $F$ in the range supported in a finite-measure set

nodes.name: Assume counterexample
nodes.statement:
For this assume that $M \subset G/H$ and $0\neq F_{0} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ with $F_0 = \chi_{M}F_0.$ Let $M_0 = \{xH \in G/H : F_{0}(xH)\neq 0 \}$. Then, 
 $$0 < \mu_{G/H}(M_0) \leq \mu_{G/H}(M) < \infty.$$
nodes.statement_short: Take $F_0$ supported in $M$ and its support $M_0$

nodes.name: Apply Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement:
By Lemma \ref{conn}, there exists $a^{(1)} \in G_0 $ satisfying 
\[
\mu_{G/H}(M) < \mu_{G/H}(M \cup a^{(1)}M_0) < \mu_{G/H}(M) + \frac{\epsilon}{2}. 
\]
nodes.statement_short: First application of Lemma 2.2

nodes.name: Iterate Lemma 2.2
nodes.statement_short: Second application of Lemma 2.2

nodes.name: Construct sequence
nodes.statement_short: Build increasing sequence $M_k$ with controlled measure

nodes.name: Finite measure of S
nodes.statement_short: Union $S$ has finite measure

nodes.name: Define translates; induction base
nodes.statement_short: Define translates $F_k$; induction base $F_1=F_0$

nodes.name: Inductive step
nodes.statement:
Let us  assume that $F_{k-1} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}),\ \text{i.e.}\  F_{k-1} = W_{\xi}(\eta)$ for some $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}.$ Then,
\begin{align*}
F_{k}(aH) &= W_{\xi}(\eta)((a^{(k-1)})^{-1}aH)\\
&=\left\langle \eta , \pi((a^{(k-1)})^{-1}aH)\xi \right\rangle\\
&= \left\langle \pi(a^{(k-1)}H)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi \right\rangle\\
&= W_{\xi}(\pi({a^{(k-1)}H)}\eta)
\end{align*}
which implies that $F_{k} \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}).$
nodes.statement_short: Translate of a range element stays in the range

nodes.name: Linear independence
nodes.statement: Using (\ref{lin-ind}), we conclude that the family $\{F_{k}\}_{k\in \mathbb{N}}$ of functions on $G/H$ is linearly independent vanishing outside the set $S$ of finite measure.
nodes.statement_short: The $F_k$ are linearly independent and vanish outside $S$

nodes.name: RKHS dimension bound
nodes.statement:
Since $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ is a reproducing kernel Hilbert space with point-wise bounded kernel, therefore each subspace of $W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi}) $ consisting of functions having support 
 on a set of finite measure must be of finite dimension \cite{Wilc:00}. If $W_{\xi}\eta \in W_{\xi}(\mathcal{H}_{\pi})$ such that $\mu_{G/H}\{xH : W_{\xi}\eta(xH)\neq 0 \}< \infty, $ then $W_{\xi}\eta = 0$ a.e. and hence $\eta = 0.$
nodes.statement_short: Finite-dimensionality of such subspaces [Wilc:00] forces $\eta=0$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: Thus, the support of $W_{\xi}\eta$ is a set of infinite measure for every non-zero $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$.
nodes.statement_short: Conclude infinite measure of support

nodes.name: Tail bound
nodes.statement:
Let $K$ be an arbitrary compact subset of $G/H$ and $K^{'}$ be a compact subset of $G/H$ such that $K\subseteq K^{'}$. Then for $\eta \in \mathcal{H}_{\pi}$ and $sH \in G/H,$ we have
\begin{align*}
&\left\|\pi(sH)\eta - C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\langle \pi(sH)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\ \pi(aH)\xi_2\  d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\right\|^2\\
&=\sup\limits_{\|\zeta\|=1}\left|\left(\left\langle  \pi(sH)\eta - C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1}\int_{s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\langle \pi(s)\eta,
\pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\right.\right. \right.\\
&\qquad\qquad \qquad \qquad \left.\times \pi(aH)\xi_2\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\right) , \left.\zeta\rangle  \right|^2\\
&=\sup\limits_{\|\zeta\|=1}\left|  C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-1} \int_{aH \notin s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\langle \pi(sH)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\right. \\
&\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad \times \left. \left\langle\pi(aH)\xi_2,\zeta \right\rangle d\mu_{G/H}(aH) \right|^{2}\\
&\leq C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-2}\int_{aH \notin s\cdot K^{'}}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\big|\langle \pi(sH)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\big|^{2}\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\\
&\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad\times \sup\limits_{\|\zeta\| = 1}\int_{G/H}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\big|\langle\pi(aH)\xi_2,\zeta \rangle\big|^2\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\\
&\leq C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-2}C_{\xi_2}\int_{aH \notin s\cdot K}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\big|\langle \pi(sH)\eta, \pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\big|^{2}\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH)\\
&\leq C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-2}C_{\xi_2}\int_{aH \notin  K}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(sa)}\right)\big|\langle \eta, \pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\big|^{2}\ d\mu_{G/H}(saH)\\
&= C_{\xi_1\xi_2}^{-2}C_{\xi_2}\int_{aH \notin K}\left(\frac{\rho(e)}{\rho(a)}\right)\big|\langle \eta, \pi(aH)\xi_1 \rangle\big|^{2}\ d\mu_{G/H}(aH).
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound truncation error by tail integral of $|W_{\xi_1}\eta|^2$ outside $K$

nodes.name: Exhaustion
nodes.statement: But, $G/H$ is $\sigma$-compact, therefore, there exists a sequence  $\{K_n\}_{n\in \mathbb{N}}$ of compact subsets of $G/H$ such that $K_n\subset K_{n+1}$  for all $n\in \mathbb{N}$ and   $G/H = \bigcup\limits_{n=1}^{\infty}K_n$.
nodes.statement_short: Exhaust $G/H$ by compacts $K_n$

nodes.statement_short: Dominated convergence

nodes.statement_short: Choose $K_n$ with small tail

nodes.statement_short: Conclude HAP

nodes.name: Well-definedness
nodes.statement:
First we show that $f_{A_1A_2}$ is well defined. For this, we compute
\begin{align*}
&\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
&\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\big|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\big|^2dt \right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
&\leq\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\left( \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 dt\right)^{\frac{1}{2}}\|\psi_2\|_{2}\ \frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
&\leq \|\psi_2\|_{2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \big|\langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \big|^2 \frac{ dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)^{1/2}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\frac{d\theta da}{a^{n+1}} \right)^{1/2}\\
&=\|\psi_2\|_{2}\sqrt{C_{\psi_1}}\|f\|_2\ n^{-\frac{1}{2}}(A_1^{-n}-A_2^{-n})< \infty.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Absolute convergence of the defining integral by Cauchy-Schwarz

nodes.name: Test function
nodes.statement_short: Integrability against test $g$

nodes.name: Tonelli
nodes.statement: Thus, using Tonneli theorem, the function  $g(\cdot)\langle f, \pi(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)\psi_1\rangle \pi(\cdot,\cdot,\cdot)\psi_2(\cdot) $ is integrable.
nodes.statement_short: Tonelli

nodes.name: Swap integrals
nodes.statement:
Again, we have
\begin{align*}
& \int_{\mathbb{R}^n} f_{A_1A_2}(x)\overline{g(x)}\ dx \\
 &= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1} \int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\left(\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\right)dx\\
 &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\left(\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\overline{g(x)}\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2(x)dx\right)\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}\\
 &=C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}}.
 \end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Fubini swap of integrals

nodes.name: Bounded functional
nodes.statement_short: Bound the pairing by $\|g\|_2$

nodes.name: Riesz
nodes.statement: Therefore, by  Riesz representation theorem $f_{A_1A_2}\in L^2(\mathbb{R}^n).$
nodes.statement_short: Riesz representation gives $f_{A_1A_2}\in L^2$

nodes.name: Plancherel
nodes.statement:
Now on using Plancherel Theorem, we have
\begin{align*}
&&&\langle f_{A_1A_2}, g\rangle &\\
 &&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} \langle f, \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_1\rangle\ \langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)\psi_2, g\rangle\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} & \\
&&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n} (f*\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_1^{\star}(t))\ (g*\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_2^{\star}(t))\ \frac{dtd\theta da}{a^{n+1}} &\\
&&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\widehat{f}(\omega)\ \widehat{\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\ \psi_1^{\star}}(\omega)\ \overline{\widehat{g}(\omega)}\ \overline{\widehat{\pi(a,r_\theta,0)\psi_2^{\star}}}(\omega)\ \frac{d\omega d\theta da}{a^{n+1}} &\\
&&&= C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\widehat{f}(\omega) \left( \int_{A_1}^{A_2}\int_{S0(n)}\overline{\widehat{\psi_1}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))}\ \widehat{\psi_2}(ar_\theta^{-1}(\omega))\ \frac{da d\theta}{a} \right) \overline{\widehat{g}(\omega)} d\omega.
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Plancherel computation

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement_short: Read off the Fourier transform

nodes.name: Define tails
nodes.statement_short: Define small- and large-scale tails

nodes.name: Error bound
nodes.statement:
Then,
\begin{align*}
&\left\|\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f(x)-\left(C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}\int_{A_1^{'}a}^{A_2^{'}a}\int_{S0(n)}\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left(\langle \pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f,\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_1\rangle\right)\right.\right.\\
&\qquad \qquad \qquad \qquad  \qquad \left.\left.\times\  \left(\pi(a_1,{r_{\theta}}_1,t_1)\psi_2(x)\right)\ \frac{dt_1d\theta_1da_1}{a_1^{n+1}}\right) \right\|_{\infty}\\
& = \Big\| f_{A_1^{'}a}(x)+ f_{A_2^{'}a}(x)  \|_{\infty} \leq  \|\widehat{f_{A_1^{'}a}}\|_{1} +  \|\widehat{f_{A_2^{'}a}}\Big\|_{1}\\
&\leq|C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|
\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left|\widehat{\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f}(\omega)\right|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}a} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))| \ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\
&\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}\left|\widehat{\pi(a,r_{\theta},t)f}(\omega)\right|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega. \\
 &\leq |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|a|^{n/2}|\widehat{f}(ar_{\theta}^{-1}\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}a} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\
&\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|a|^{n/2}|\widehat{f}(ar_{\theta}^{-1}\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}a}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega\\
&\leq |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|p|^{-n/2}|\widehat{f}(\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{0}^{A_1^{'}} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega \\
&\qquad+ |C_{\psi_1\psi_2}^{-1}|\int_{\mathbb{R}^n}|p|^{-n/2}|\widehat{f}(\omega)|\int_{S0(n)}\int_{A_2^{'}}^{\infty} |\widehat{\psi_{1}}(a_1{r_\theta}_1^{-1}(\omega))\ \widehat{\psi_2}(a_1 {r_{\theta}}_1^{-1}(\omega))|\ \frac{da_1d\theta_1}{a_1}d\omega.  
\end{align*}
nodes.statement_short: Bound error by $L^1$ norms of tail Fourier transforms

nodes.statement: Therefore, we can choose  $0 < A_1\leq A_2$ such that for any $(a,r_{\theta},t)$ with $0< p\leq a$ and  $0< A_1^{'}\leq A_1, A_2<A_2^{'}$, the conclusion of the theorem holds.

nodes.name: Projection bound
nodes.statement:
Let $P_R :L^2(G) \to L^2(G) $ be the orthogonal projection from $L^2(G)$ to the closed subspace $W_{\psi}(L^2(A))$ and $P_M :L^2(G) \to L^2(G)$ be the orthogonal projection from $L^2(G)$ to the closed subspace of functions with support contained in $M.$ Now, 
\begin{align} \| W_{\psi}f - \chi_{M}\cdot W_{\psi}f\| &= \| W_{\psi}f- P_MP_R(W_{\psi}f)\| \nonumber \\ \nonumber
& \geq \|W_{\psi}f\| - \|P_MP_R\|\ \|W_{\psi}f\|\\
&= (1-\|P_MP_R\|)\ \sqrt{C_{\psi}}\ \|f\|.
\end{align}
nodes.section: 4 Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Introduce projections and bound by $1-\|P_MP_R\|$

nodes.name: Norm of P_M P_R
nodes.statement:
From \cite{hal;78}, the operator norm $\|P_MP_R\|$  is given by
\begin{flalign*}
\| P_MP_R\|^{2} &= \int_{G}\int_{G}|\chi_{M}(b,a)\ k((b^{'},a^{'}),(b,a))|^2\ d\mu(b,a)\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})&\\
&=\int_{G}\int_{G}|\chi_{M}(b,a)\frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\langle \psi_{ba}, \psi_{b^{'}a^{'}}\rangle |^2\ d\mu(b,a)\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})&\\
&=\frac{1}{C_{\psi}^2}\int_{M} \int_{G}|W_{\psi}\psi_{ba}(b^{'},a^{'})|^2\ d\mu(b^{'},a^{'})\ d\mu(b,a)&\\
&=\frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\int_{M}\|\psi_{ba}\|^2\ d\mu(b,a)&\\
&= \frac{1}{C_{\psi}}\|\psi\|^{2}\ \mu(M).
\end{flalign*}
nodes.section: 4 Wavelet group of the form $B\ltimes A$
nodes.statement_short: Hilbert-Schmidt norm computation gives $\|P_MP_R\|^2=\|\psi\|^2\mu(M)/C_\psi$

nodes.name: Conclude
nodes.statement: On substituting the value $\|P_MP_R\|$ into (\ref{conc}), we get the desired inequality.

nodes.name: Cauchy-Schwarz
nodes.statement:
Using Lemma \ref{isom} and  Cauchy-Schwarz inequality, it follows that
\begin{flalign} &\left(\int_B\int_{L}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|t|^2|W_{\psi}f(b,l,t)|^2 \delta_{\tau}(b) dl\ dt\ db\right)^{1/2}\nonumber &\\
& \times \left(\int_B\int_{\widehat{L}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}|\gamma|^2\|(\delta, \gamma)W_{\psi}f(b,\cdot,\cdot)\|_{\text{HS}}^2\ \delta_{\tau}(b) d\delta\ d\gamma\ db \right)^{1/2} \geq\frac{1}{2}C_{\psi}\|f\|^2.
 \end{flalign}
